noteEn: The year has 24 {ko:절기}, solar terms, about 15 days apart. They follow the sun through the year. They are a calendar shared across East Asia. UNESCO inscribed The Twenty-Four Solar Terms for China in 2016.

notes: Pass 1, author (content-skill): note, items and sources written from the cited pages, all accessed 2026-10-30; every claim is quoted in quoteOrLocator.

Pass 2, three checkers. Language: romanization of every item and token is the F-CNT-002 converter's output (checked by the build); polite 해요 register in the ko text; Pre-A1 English. Culture and facts: each claim matched to an allowlisted source (§6.6) with the §5.1 conventions. Shared East Asian heritage is not framed as Korean in origin (§5.1): the note calls the terms a calendar shared across East Asia and names UNESCO's element for China, inscribed 2016, under its UNESCO name. 'About 15 days apart' reads the KASI table (23 Oct, 7 Nov, 22 Nov, 7 Dec); 'follow the sun' restates UNESCO's 'the sun's annual circular motion'. Learning design: 5 items, at most 8 new (lesson-new-load), no two items of the drop said alike (dictation-unambiguous), no %, score, age word, speaking line or emoji (review-copy).

Pass 3, reviser and third pass: fixes of pass 2 applied (wording kept plain, every holiday and term date re-read against the KASI table), es and ko overlays re-read against the English; no copy claims native-speaker or expert review.
